subject: Sandbox→Prod IaC hardening & ops checklist — pre-release checkin
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Rivera <infra-eng@acme-payments.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <procurement@acme-payments.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Sandbox→Prod IaC hardening & ops checklist — pre-release checkin

Alex / team —

Thanks for the quick sync earlier. As we move the private deployment from sandbox into your production VPC next week, we want to make sure the IaC bundle and release gating meet both your operational and compliance requirements. Draft materials attached below.

High-level asks:
- Can Acme confirm the egress/NAT constraints in the region we discussed (us-west-2)? We propose an outbound-only NAT with strict CIDR allowlists for telemetry endpoints.
- Review the terraform module contract changes (link and diff attached) — we introduced a new network_module/v2 that separates control-plane subnets from workload subnets. We need approval on the subnet sizing and ephemeral IP allocation.
- Helm values: default replicas, liveness/readiness thresholds, and resource requests have been tightened. Confirm these are acceptable for your staging traffic profile.
- Ansible hardening tasks (ssh lockdown, kubelet flags) are in section 4 of the playbook — security team will want to run the provided checklist during the preflight.

Attached (stubs):
- priv-deploy-hardening-playbook-v1.2.pdf (PDF, 420KB) — narrative + checklist
- terraform-module-contracts-diff.patch (text, 12KB) — diff against v1 modules
- helm-values-examples.yaml (yaml, 3KB) — recommended values for canary + prod

Timeline: we’re aiming to run a protected dry-run on July 3, and a controlled cutover window July 8–9. Please flag any blockers by EOD Friday (Jul 2) so we can delay if needed.

Next steps I’ll take after your review: open a JIRA for remaining infra action items and publish a read-only runbook link for your on-call team.

Thanks —
Marissa
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Rivera <infra-eng@acme-payments.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <procurement@acme-payments.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sandbox→Prod IaC hardening & ops checklist — pre-release checkin

Marissa — thanks for the package. A couple things from our side before we sign off on the dry-run: 

Questions / clarifications:
1) NAT / egress: your proposed outbound-only NAT sounds fine, but we need to confirm whether the telemetry endpoints are behind a CDN with stable IP ranges. If IPs can change frequently we’ll need a proxy in our VPC to avoid frequent ACL churn.

2) Control-plane separation: the subnet sizing in network_module/v2 looks tighter than our current template. What happens if a control-plane node needs to scale unexpectedly (maintenance events)? Is there an automated fallback to burst IP allocation or cross-AZ failover?

3) KMS/HSM: We saw references to KMS key rotation in the playbook but not to HSM-backed key wraps for customer-managed keys. Acme requires FIPS 140-2 validated wrapping for keys used to protect token caches. Can you confirm support or provide a migration path?

Also — can you attach a minimal network diagram that includes the VPC CIDRs, transit gateway, and the proposed proxy/egress path? That will go to our security review board.

Appreciate the timeline. We’ll triage internally and aim to give formal feedback by Jul 2 EOD.

—Alex
Senior SRE, Acme Payments

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 07:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sandbox→Prod IaC hardening & ops checklist — pre-release checkin

Alex — thanks for the detailed questions. Answers inline below.

> 1) NAT / egress: your proposed outbound-only NAT sounds fine, but we need to confirm whether the telemetry endpoints are behind a CDN with stable IP ranges. If IPs can change frequently we’ll need a proxy in our VPC to avoid frequent ACL churn.

- Response: The telemetry endpoints (metrics.redwood-inference.com and logs.redwood-inference.com) are fronted by a CDN. We publish an AS-SET and a short-lived IP prefix document. To avoid ACL churn we recommend the proxy approach you mentioned; we include an optional terraform module (network/proxy_gateway) that deploys an internal proxy backed by an EKS pod with stable ENIs. See network-diagram-vpc.png (attached).

> 2) Control-plane separation: the subnet sizing in network_module/v2 looks tighter than our current template. What happens if a control-plane node needs to scale unexpectedly (maintenance events)? Is there an automated fallback to burst IP allocation or cross-AZ failover?

- Response: network_module/v2 reserves a small AZ-spanning /26 per control-plane pool as a warm standby for burst allocation and supports automatic reallocation to a secondary AZ via the terraform modules we added (module.network.reallocate_on_pressure = true). If you prefer we can include an optional dynamic-routed transit attachment to allow cross-AZ failover for short windows (we flagged that in the diff).

> 3) KMS/HSM: We saw references to KMS key rotation in the playbook but not to HSM-backed key wraps for customer-managed keys. Acme requires FIPS 140-2 validated wrapping for keys used to protect token caches. Can you confirm support or provide a migration path?

- Response: We currently support AWS CloudHSM for key wrapping; the playbook step 3.2 includes a scripted key-wrap migration (ansible/tasks/kms_hsm_migrate.yml) and a validation runbook (docs/sops/priv-deploy-hardening#kms-hsm). If you want, we can provide an HSM-backed proof-of-concept run in a staging VPC during the dry-run.

I’ve attached the requested network diagram and a short terraform snippet that shows the proxy module usage. I also created a JIRA to track follow-ups: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-4821 (filters: network/proxy, kms-hsm).

Attachments (stubs):
- network-diagram-vpc.png (PNG, 480KB)
- proxy-module-example.tf (text, 2KB)

If this addresses the security board’s needs we can mark the network and KMS sections as "ready for review" and proceed with the dry-run.

—Irene
Senior Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

All — quick procurement note: we reviewed the SOW annex for private deployment and confirm budget for the July cutover window. Legal will circulate a redline for the infra attachment (expect by Mon Jul 5).

Two small asks from procurement side:
- Please include an explicit SLA clause for incident response time during the first 30 days of production (we typically require a 1-hour P1 response).
- Add an export-control classification paragraph to the deploy notes (we need it for our internal audit).

If you can add those two items to the annex and resend the doc we’ll fast-track signatures. Otherwise onboarding is on track.

Thanks —
Priya
Procurement Manager, Acme Payments
